name: What is the difference between renovation and build-out for commercial space?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between renovating an existing commercial space and doing a full build-out?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between renovating an existing commercial space and doing a full build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: A renovation improves an existing commercial space that already has some usable layout, systems, or finishes in place. A build-out goes further and turns a shell, raw interior, or fully gutted space into a functional tenant-ready environment. Build-outs often require more extensive work because the contractor may need to install walls, ceilings, lighting, HVAC distribution, plumbing, electrical, restrooms, finishes, and life-safety components from the ground up. Renovations can still be complex, but they usually start with more of the infrastructure already in place. The difference matters because build-outs are typically more schedule-intensive and can require more upfront coordination with design, permitting, and landlord approvals. Owners should know which category their project fits before budgeting or selecting a contractor. That classification affects cost expectations, inspection planning, and how much hidden-condition risk to expect.
acceptedAnswer.description: Renovation usually means improving an existing space, while build-out means creating a tenant-ready space from a shell or stripped interior. Build-outs often require more trade coordination, more permits, and more time because major systems and layouts may need to be installed from scratch.
